analyst_view.overall: Cologne (14th, 10 points, no win in five) host promoted Elversberg (9th, 13 points), a game local outlets call a duel between equals. Cologne's injury list is long: striker Thijs Dallinga (cruciate ligament), Ellyes Skhiri, Timo Hübers, Rav van den Berg, Imad Rondic and, newly, Alessio Castro-Montes are out, and the numbers now count all of these, taking roughly a fifth off Cologne's goals. Ragnar Ache is fit again and goalkeeper Marvin Schwäbe missed the start of the week with back problems, so Ron-Robert Zieler could play (one site lists Schwäbe as doubtful). Elversberg, coached by Vincent Wagner, play an open, attacking game and have conceded 11 in five, most recently losing 1-0 at Freiburg; captain Lukas Pinckert and Jan Gyamerah are back. No referee is named yet; I found nothing the numbers can't see, so I stay with them on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, down from 2.8 a day ago because they now take off Cologne's absentees, mainly Dallinga (about -11%), Skhiri and Castro-Montes. Elversberg's leaky, open defence suits Cologne's breakers El Mala, Moore and Maina, and Ache is back up front, while a possible switch from Schwäbe to Zieler in goal is only a doubt. These pull both ways, so I stay at 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners, most of them Cologne's (7.1), and they already count both teams' recent corner form. Cologne mostly attack on the break, which can mean fewer corners than that split suggests, but Elversberg concede plenty and Ache gives Cologne a target for crosses. Nothing new in the news, so I stay at 11.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already add some for both teams' recent bookings (Cologne 16 in six, Elversberg 10). No referee is named yet and this is not a derby or a heated fixture, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots and already trim a few for Cologne's quieter recent attacking. Elversberg's open play should give Cologne room to shoot on the break, and Elversberg themselves had more of the ball at Freiburg, so I see no reason to move and stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Ache's return gives Cologne a proper centre-forward with Dallinga out, but the numbers already reflect Cologne's recent attacking, and Elversberg missed their two big chances at Freiburg. Nothing new either way, so I stay at 8.8.
